title: Hall Overton's death
summary: Gil recalls composer Hall Overton, who sipped steadily and died of a hemorrhage two weeks earlier.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: But you don't have to become, you know, some people think of a quart a day as somebody sprawled in the gutter. There are lots of people who drink a quart a day. A fellow, a composer just died two weeks ago from doing just that thing. Hall Overton was his name.

He's been associated with jazz. He was a white man from the Mid-West. But he's been in New York for some twenty years and he orchestrated some of Monk's Town Hall things. He did a concert at Lake Tahoe and he'd been a private composition teacher for a long time. And also teaches at Julliard ego. And a couple of weeks, I got a 'phone call from his girl saying that he wanted to see
me and named (a couple of his).... I didn't know him very well, but he'd been on the, a couple of boards. I think he was on the National Endowment Board. I think he was, do you know him?

I think he was on that board. Or the Guggenheim (Schenckheim?), one or the other, because I met him on the subway I'd say about three months ago and of course you know how much noise the subway makes when you're trying to say something. I don't remember exactly what, how did you like your award or your grant, you know. A funny question to ask, you know. Apparently why he was asking me was because he was on it and was responsible for it.
Had something to do with you getting it, yes. (LAUGHTER).

But he sipped like that while he composed. All his life he had done that and it ruined his liver. And he got a hemorrhage of the esophagus or something and was taken to the hospital. And when I went to see him, he wasn't allowed to have any visitors and the next thing I knew, he was dead. From Always lived that. A respectable, productive life.
